Using AI and stream processing tools, the system cleans, analyzes, and fuses information to create accurate traffic scenarios. These scenarios are then simulated in MATLAB, allowing engineers to test solutions before real-world deployment. We used three models: pothole, barricade, and construction zone. The pothole model creates surface depressions that make vehicles slow down or adjust. The barricade model adds temporary obstacles like cones or barriers to divert traffic. The construction zone model combines blocked lanes, warning signs, and barricades to simulate roadside maintenance. MATLAB’s Automated Driving Toolbox and driving Scenario functions parse the imported data into structured objects like roads, lanes, and actors.
